title: Probabilities of Causation in Nondeterministic Causal Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.18245v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study probabilities of causation in nondeterministic causal models, where mechanisms may remain intrinsically stochastic even after all latent variables are fixed. Focusing on binary treatments and outcomes, we develop a generic identification program that represents observational and interventional data as moment constraints on latent stochastic mechanism types and computes minimal/maximal values of counterfactual quantities via constrained optimization. Within this framework, we derive sharp analytic bounds on the probabilities of causation under several assumptions tailored to nondeterministic models. Resulting identification regions are often more informative than those attainable under deterministic alternatives. We illustrate the practical relevance of these results in a case study on personalized treatment decisions and experiments on semi-synthetic datasets. translated_title: 非确定性因果模型中的因果概率
translated_abstract: 我们研究非确定性因果模型中的因果概率，在这类模型中，即使所有潜在变量都被固定，机制本身仍可能保持内在的随机性。聚焦于二元处理和结果，我们开发了一个通用的识别程序，将观察性数据和干预性数据表示为对潜在随机机制类型的矩约束，并通过约束优化计算反事实量的最小值和最大值。在该框架内，我们在若干专为非确定性模型量身定制的假设下，推导出因果概率的尖锐解析界。所得的识别区域往往比确定性替代方法所能获得的识别区域具有更丰富的信息。我们通过一个关于个性化治疗决策的案例研究以及在半合成数据集上的实验，展示了这些结果的实际意义。我们的结果阐明了经典界与非确定性因果模型之间的关系。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个面向非确定性因果模型的通用识别框架，通过矩约束与约束优化推导出因果概率的尖锐解析界，所得识别区域通常比确定性模型下的经典结果更具信息量。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a generic identification framework for nondeterministic causal models that derives sharp analytic bounds on probabilities of causation via moment constraints and constrained optimization, yielding identification regions that are often more informative than classical deterministic bounds.
